filename: Implicit learning of convective organization explains precipitation stochasticity.pdf
title: Implicit learning of convective organization explains precipitation stochasticity
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
testbed_rationale: Uses global storm-resolving DYAMOND Phase 2 simulation data coarse-grained to GCM resolution (~130 km) to parameterize subgrid convective organization and precipitation extremes, with open code on GitHub.
pain_points: Coarse-scale variables alone fail to predict precipitation variability and extreme precipitation (R^2 ~ 0.45).
In climate models, high-resolution fields are unavailable at runtime to extract organization metrics directly, requiring prognostic or memory-based prediction of latent organization variables.
Non-Gaussian distribution and heavy tails of precipitation make accurate modeling of extremes difficult.
extraction_notes: The ML model couples a rotationally-invariant convolutional autoencoder on subgrid precipitable water anomalies to extract latent organization variables (org) and a feed-forward neural network to predict coarse-grained precipitation. Offline evaluations are performed; online coupling is proposed for future implementation in GCMs.
